name: BANGLADESH

flag.title: Flag of Bangladesh
flag.note: Green field, red disc offset to centre

lead: Bangladesh is a low-lying land where three great rivers fan into the world's largest delta. More people live here than in Russia, squeezed into a country smaller than England. The Sundarbans — the planet's biggest mangrove forest — hides swimming tigers. Rice paddies turn every flat field brilliant green each monsoon.
geo: Bangladesh sits almost entirely on a giant river delta — flat, green, crisscrossed by over 700 rivers. Every monsoon, floods cover a third of the land but deposit rich mud making the soil incredibly fertile.

In the south-west, the Sundarbans mangrove forest straddles the border with India. Its tangle of roots and tidal creeks stretches 10,200 km² — the world's largest mangrove and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
animals: The Royal Bengal Tiger is Bangladesh's national animal. About 125 tigers roam the Sundarbans, swimming between islands through salty channels — the only sea-swimming tiger population on the planet.

The Hilsa (Ilish) is the national fish and a cultural treasure. Bangladesh supplies 86 % of the world's Hilsa catch. Fishers say those from the Padma River taste the finest — rich, fatty, and beloved at every feast.
culture: Bengali culture revolves around music, poetry, and rice. Rabindranath Tagore — born in this region — wrote thousands of songs; his poem became Bangladesh's national anthem. The spring festival Pahela Baishakh fills streets with bright orange-and-white clothes.

Dhaka is famous for Jamdani weaving — a UNESCO-listed craft where weavers create shimmering floral muslin entirely from memory. Bangladesh is also the world's second-largest garment exporter, clothing billions of people globally.
history: For centuries this was the heart of Bengal — a wealthy rice-and-muslin kingdom prized by Mughal emperors and British traders alike. The British East India Company made Dhaka a cloth capital, though exploitation slowly drained its wealth.

In 1971, Bangladesh fought a nine-month Liberation War for independence from Pakistan. After tremendous loss of life, victory came on 16 December — still celebrated as Victory Day — making it one of the world's youngest nations.
wows: Bangladesh is home to the world's largest river delta, where the Ganges and Brahmaputra meet the sea.
The Sundarbans' tigers swim in saltwater and hunt at sea — no other tiger population does this.
Bangladesh produces 86 % of the entire world's supply of Hilsa fish.
Dhaka has around 44,000 people per km² — one of the densest cities on Earth, per UN Habitat data.
Mughal emperors called Dhaka muslin 'woven air'; the craft is now UNESCO-listed heritage.
The Padma Bridge (2022) is 6.15 km long, built entirely with Bangladesh's own funds.
Tagore's poems became the national anthems of two nations — Bangladesh AND India.

myths.fact: Seasonal floods cover a third of the land but deposit rich silt, making soil so fertile that farmers grow three rice crops a year. Floods are a lifeline, not only a disaster.

myths.myth: It's one of the poorest nations
myths.fact: Bangladesh has lifted millions from poverty since 1990, becoming a lower-middle-income country and the world's second-largest garment exporter.
